JAK1 full-length models

Five models of P23458, 1,154 residues · Cα cartoon trace via 3Dmol.js · drag to rotate, scroll to zoom

Three full-length models. JAK1 is the only protein in this project with a published open/closed pair — the two models Jeanpierre/Debeaupuis built and used for the ΔΔG features in their own clustering. Everywhere else the pair had to be assembled from our own runs.

Shan 2014 supplies an independent closed JH2–JH1 reference; the Jeanpierre closed model sits 11.7 Å from it after a JH2 fit — agreement on the arrangement, not on the details.

The AlphaFold DB model is open for JAK1 (FERM–JH1 92.2 Å, 3.44 Å from the Jeanpierre open model) — as for JAK2, and unlike TYK2 and JAK3 where it is closed. The default AlphaFold state splits two-and-two across this family.

Jeanpierre closedAlphaFold DB v630.7780.961.580.321.350.52
Jeanpierre openAlphaFold DB v64.173.441.660.250.720.49

This is the cleanest pair in the project. Both states come from the same authors, built for the same purpose, and the per-domain RMSDs between them are 0.25–1.39 Å — the two structures differ in where JH1 sits and little else. No predictor or template confound, unlike TYK2 (AF3 closed vs AF3 open from different jobs) and JAK3 (AF3 closed vs OpenFold open).

And yet ddg_delta computed on this pair still scored AUC 0.4966 — chance. That is the strongest form of the negative result: the feature fails even when the structures are exactly what the method intends.

6. AlphaFold DB PAE

Our OpenFold runs use model_1, which emits no PAE. The AlphaFold DB download includes it, and it is the most important caveat on this page. PAE at (i, j) is the error AlphaFold expects in residue j's position when the prediction is aligned on residue i — so the off-diagonal blocks measure confidence in the relative placement of two domains, which per-residue pLDDT cannot express.

Within domains AlphaFold is confident (2.4–5.4 Å). Between FERM and JH1 it is at 21.0 Å, 68% of the 31 Å ceiling — it has essentially no idea where JH1 sits. That does not invalidate a dual-state ΔΔG, since ΔΔG is local and the domains themselves are confidently modelled, but the interface residues that generate the difference between states are in the least certain part of the model.
